info.title: RAYNET CRM API
info.description:
Cloud CRM REST API is a programming interface of the RAYNET CRM system that allows you to work with data inside the CRM system from third-party applications. Communication is done using the standard HTTP protocol with respect to [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) principles.
## Connection to RAYNET CRM
The communication protocol is HTTP, so you can use any application or library that supports this protocol. The [curl](https://curl.haxx.se/) application will be used for the demonstration. An alternative is, for example, the add-on [Talend API Tester](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/talend-api-tester-free-ed/aejoelaoggembcahagimdiliamlcdmfm) for Google Chrome. Access is secured with basic authentication (username and API key) and encrypted with TLSv1.2 and higher (HTTPS) to ensure maximum security. In the request header you must send the name of your instance (e.g. `my-crm`).

```bash
  curl -X GET -u 'user:api-key' -H 'X-Instance-Name: my-crm' 'https://app.raynet.cz/api/v2/company/'
```

## Data types

The values of individual attributes in the RAYNET CRM system are made up of several basic data types:

+ `String` - Text value.

+ `Number` - Numeric value. Depending on the context, this can be either an integer or a decimal number. Decimal numbers use a decimal point.

+ `Truth value` - YES/NO value. For the YES value you can use true, on, yes and 1; for the NO value you can use false, off, no and 0.

+ `Date` - Date as a string in the format `yyyy-MM-dd`.

+ `Date and time` - Date and time as a string in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. Date and time in ISO8601 format are also accepted (e.g. `2022-01-01T12:00:00.000+01:00`).

+ `Reference` - The reference data type refers to another record in the RAYNET CRM system. In the incoming data, the reference is a map (JavaScript object) that contains the keys:

  + id - Identifier of the referenced record.


### Date and time

The date and time as a string in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` is in the time zone of the user through whom the API requests are made. For filtering and writing (`PUT`, `POST`) it is possible to use both formats (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, ISO8601).

In response, the date and time is formatted as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` in the user's time zone by default. By adding the parameter `dateFormat=ISO8601` it is possible to influence the output format, the value will be formatted into the form `2022-01-01T12:00:00.000+01:00`.
e.g. `https://ww....company/?dateFormat=ISO8601`

## List filtering

Operators working on attributes and values are as follows:

+ `EQ` - Test for equality of values.
+ `EQ_OR_NULL` - Test for equality or empty value.

+ `NE` - Test for inequality of values.

+ `NE_OR_NULL` - Test for inequality or empty value.

+ `LT` - The value in the database is less than the one entered.

+ `LE` - The value in the database is less than or equal to the one entered.

+ `GT` - The value in the database is greater than the one entered.

+ `GE` - The value in the database is greater than or equal to the one entered.

+ `LIKE` - Test for a value matching an expression (e.g. the ABC% filter value finds all records that start with the characters ABC).

+ `LIKE_NOCASE` - Similar to LIKE, but case insensitive.

+ `IN` - Test for equality of (multiple) values separated by comma. The correct input format is e.g. `1,2,3,4`.

+ `NOT_IN` - Test for inequality of (multiple) values separated by comma. The correct input format is e.g. `1,2,3,4`.

+ `CUSTOM` - Special operator - the test behavior is described later in the documentation.

The default operator is the equality `EQ`. The operator is written in square brackets after the attribute name. It is thus possible to enter multiple filtering criteria over the same attribute. `https://app..../?validFrom[GT]="2014-06-01"&validTill[LT]="2014-06-10"`
A common scenario is to filter out all records that have the attribute empty or non-empty. For this purpose, the value `empty string` can be used in combination with the `EQ` or `NE` operator.

## List layout

The layout of the list is controlled by the `sortColumn` and `sortDirection` parameters. For each API, there is a list of values that can be used to sort the list. The `sortDirection` parameter can have the values:

+ `ASC` - Values are sorted in ascending order

+ `DESC` - Values are sorted in descending order

## List pagination

The list can be paginated by setting the `offset` and `limit` parameters. Offset specifies the first record to be displayed, limit specifies the number of records. The maximum page size is 1 000 items. Například `https://app..../?offset=0&limit=2`

## Fulltext

In most of the lists, you can use full-text search according to the entered text string. The `fulltext` parameter is used for this purpose. It is applied e.g. as follows: `https://app..../?fulltext=sometext`

## API limits

Each API response contains headers that describe the API usage status for the given instance.

```
curl -X GET -u 'user:api-key' -H 'X-Instance-Name: my-crm' 'https://app.raynet.cz/api/v2/company/'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Status: 200 OK
X-Ratelimit-Limit: 24000
X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 23999
X-Ratelimit-Reset: 1508889600
```

The meaning of each header is as follows:

| Header | Meaning |
| -------- | ------ |
| X-Ratelimit-Limit | Total limit for the current time window and instance.
| X-Ratelimit-Remaining | Remaining number of requests. |
| X-Ratelimit-Reset | Time when the time window will expire and the limit will be reset. The value indicates [Unix time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time). |

If the limit is exceeded, an error message is returned with the HTTP code `429 Too Many Requests`:

```json
{

  "type": "RequestLimitReached",

  "message": "API request limit reached. See the X-RateLimit-* headers and check out the API documentation for more details."

}
```

### What if my limits aren't enough

By default, access is limited to 24,000 requests per day (counted from midnight to the next midnight in the UTC time zone). In case the limit is not enough for your integration, contact our customer support at podpora@raynet.cz and we will surely find a suitable solution together.

### Rest API Limits
The API returns an HTTP status code 429 Too Many Requests if a single client exceeds the limit of 4 concurrently active connections. This restriction is implemented as part of fair-use policies aimed at ensuring service stability and equal access for all users. Recommendations: 
  + If a higher number of requests is needed, consider using a queue, for example.
  + Ensure efficient use of connections, including proper closure and reuse.

### Wrong login

If more than 20 requests are sent with incorrect login information, this access will be blocked for 60 minutes. This restriction applies to the specific IP address.

tags.name: Custom buttons
tags.description:
## configuration

You can use the Custom Actions Button to run integration scenarios created by programmers fully custom or on platforms such as https://www.make.com/. Buttons can also open external URLs or trigger actions. These will fill out and download a custom print report, initiate a call on your phone, or send data to another cloud app.

You can configure the buttons yourself in the administration of your CRM system, in the section "For developers -> Custom action buttons".

The parameters of custom action button are:

| Attribute | Description | Note |
| -------- | ------ | ------ |
| Name | Button name | | |
| URL | URL template | It is possible to use the variables `{token}`, `{entityId}`, `{entityName}`, `{userName}`, `{userId}`, `{personId}`, `{extId_$extIdCode}` see below |
| Location | Where the button appears | The options are `Main Menu`, `List`, `Detail` |
| Record | Entity name where the button should be displayed | Only for placement in list or record detail |
| Description | Button description | Only for placement in a list or record detail. Appears when there are two or more buttons for one entity.
| Action | Action type | `OPEN URL`, `AJAX`, `DOWNLOAD` see below |
| Method | Type of http request | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` Only for `AJAX` and `DOWNLOAD` type actions |
| Refresh data after | Time in ms | Only available for `List` and `Detail`. The CRM system will update the displayed data after the specified time |
| Success header | Header of the message shown after successful action | Only for `AJAX` |
| Success text | Text of the message shown after successful action | Only for `AJAX` |
| Require confirmation before running | A confirmation dialog will be shown to the user before running the action |  |
| Visible only to administrator |Can only be seen by administrator |  |
| Require saving the record | The record must be saved before the action is ran | Only available for `Detail` |
| Open in | Open URL in a new tab or in a new window | The options are `OPEN_TAB` and `OPEN_WINDOW`. Only available for `OPEN URL` action. |
| Width | Width of newly opened window | Only available for `OPEN URL` action with `OPEN_WINDOW` option. |
| Height | Height of newly opened window | Only available for `OPEN URL` action with `OPEN_WINDOW` option. |
| Restore data after closing the window | Restore detail or list tab after closing the window | Only available for `OPEN URL` action with `OPEN_WINDOW` option and `List` or `Detail` location.

URL parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
| -------- | ------ |
| token | Security token generated by CRM system. It can be verified using the API (see below) |
| entityId | ID of the record from which the action is triggered. Only available for `Detail` |
| entityName | Name of the entity from which the action is triggered. Only available for `Detail` and `List` |
| userName | Email of the user who triggers the action.
| userId | ID of the user who triggers the action. Users can be filtered using the `list of contacts` API with the `userAccount-id` parameter |
| personId | ID of the contact who triggered the action. The contact can be filtered using the `contact detail` API with the `id` parameter |
| extId_$extIdCode | Value of the external id in the record from which the action is triggered. Only available for `Detail`. E.g. in case of external id "myid:123" enter extId_myid |

If the action is run from `List` and a method other than `GET` is used, the IDs of the selected (if any) or displayed records are sent within the `RequestBody` (always).

Action:

| Action | Description |
| -------- | ------ |
| OPEN URL | Open URL in a new tab |
| AJAX | Asynchronous request. Upon successful processing, HTTP 200 and `{success: true}` must be returned. If an error occurs, it is possible to return JSON in the format `{"success": false, "message": "An error has occurred"}` |
| DOWNLOAD | File Download |

tags.name: External identifier
tags.description:
As part of record identification, it is possible to use an external identifier that can be stored for a specific record. 
Based on this identifier, the record can then be traced (call the API for the detail of this record). Each record can have up to 10 external identifiers.

The identifier should have a prefix indicating its origin (or the system it comes from). This is useful when integrating multiple systems so that the identifiers are unambiguous. For example, the external identifier can be `erp:123455`.

The external identifier can be written using a directly designated API to an existing record (see below) or can be sent at the same time as the record is created. For example, when creating an Account, it is possible to write the external identifier as follows:

```
curl -X PUT 'api/v2/company'

{

  "name": "COMPANYNAME LLC",

  "rating": "A",

  "state": "A_POTENTIAL",

  "role": "B_PARTNER",

  "extId": "erp:123455"

} 
```

The detail of the record can then be retrieved using the URL: `/api/v2/{entityName}/ext/{extId}/` (https://app.raynet.cz/api/v2/company/ext/erp:123456/)

tags.name: Webhook
tags.description:
Webhook is a tool for sending notifications about changes in your CRM system to an external system via HTTP protocol. Notifications are sent as POST requests to the selected URLs.

Configuration is done in RAYNET CRM settings in the _Webhook_ section. You can set up multiple URLs for sending requests and specify the following for each one:

* event types to be sent,

* the security code that will be sent with each request in the `X-RAYNETCRM-Token` header.

The configuration also includes a technical contact, which is a set of emails to which an email will be sent in case of problems. It will be sent in the following cases:

* Your URL has not received notifications for more than 1 day (server is unavailable or returns HTTP code other than `2xx`).

* Your URL is receiving requests again, if point 1 has occurred.

* Your URL has not received requests for more than 7 days. Webhook will be deactivated and removed from the settings.

Internally, outgoing notifications from the CRM system are queued. If the destination URLs are available, they are sent repeatedly. Therefore, you will not lose any events when the external system is down.

By default, the sending rate is limited to 2 events per second per configured URL. The interval between sending dynamically changes based on the queue length - from 500 ms (with a long queue of 100+ requests) to 5 s (with an empty queue). The first request in the queue is sent immediately. At the same time the maximum processing time of the webhook is limited (connectTimeout - 10s, socketTimeout - 60s). After the connection, you will wait a maximum of 60 seconds for a response.

### supported events

**record.created**

The event is sent after a new record is created. The data includes the record type and the id. The external ID is also included, if defined for the record.

```json
{

   "eventId": "62497f2c609d4b7184b9adf1e427fa55",

   "createdAt": "2017-01-18T13:16:39.923+01:00",

   "type": "record.created",

   "author": "admin@domain.rnt",

   "source": {

      "name": "user",

      "description": "browser"

   },

   "data": {

      "entityName": "Company",

      "entityId": 123,

      "extIds": [

          "1111"

      ]

   }

}
```

**record.updated**

The event is sent after the record is changed.

```json
{

   "eventId": "d3ba342896d94dd5a4ee72d998e1e7c4",

   "createdAt": "2017-01-19T14:02:31.123+01:00",

   "type": "record.updated",

   "author": "admin@domain.rnt",

   "source": {

      "name": "user",

      "description": "browser"

   },

   "data": {

      "entityName": "Company",

      "entityId": 2,

      "extIds": null

   }

}
```

**record.deleted**

The event is sent after the record is deleted.

```json
{

   "eventId": "22b1d9c792814537b574e053642f2ce6",

   "createdAt": "2017-02-02T11:45:00.873+01:00",

   "type": "record.deleted",

   "author": "admin@domain.rnt",

   "source": {

      "name": "user",

      "description": "browser"

   },

   "data": {

      "entityName": "Company",

      "entityId": 2,

      "extIds": null

   }

}
```

### event source

The `source` key, identifying the source of the action that triggered the event, is part of the event. The possible values of the `name` nested attribute are:

* `user`: the event is the result of a user action. The `description` field is then either `browser` (CRM in a browser) or `mobile` (mobile application).

* `api`: the event was generated based on an API request. If API key login was used, `description` contains the name of the API key.

* Other events are marked as `system`.

Converts a lead into records in the contact database (Accounts, Contacts) and optionally into a Deal.
The request body may include `company`, `person` and/or `businessCase`.

The following rules apply:
- At least one of `company`, `person`, or `businessCase` must be provided.
- If `businessCase` is provided, `company` and `person` values in the request are ignored — the Account and Contact linked to the Deal are used for the conversion.
- If only `person` is provided without `company`, the Account from the person's primary relationship will be linked (if available).

The `businessCase` field is optional and can be used to link the conversion to an existing Deal.

The API is used for:

a) creating an attachment record linking to any URL, e.g. a website. The attachment is added to the selected entity, specified by its ID and entity name. To function, the API needs to know the URL of the link and the name of the link.
```

  { "link": "https://raynet.cz", "linkName": "raynet.cz"}

```
b) creating an attachment record that references a previously uploaded file.  The attachment is added to the selected entity, specified by its ID and entity name.  To function, the API needs to know the UUID of the preloaded file along with other parameters of that file.
```

  {"fileName":"upload.bin","uuid":"0cd5d016-f534-4093-943b-740961b03b6f","contentType":"application/octet-stream","fileSize":21195}

```
c) creating an attachment record that references a folder from Documents library.  The attachment is added to the selected entity, specified by its ID and entity name.  To function, the API needs to know the ID of folder
```
  { "folderId": 6 }
```
